Article Title: 'Don't waste court's time': SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana
Article Text:
SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to grant an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the release of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, observing that those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the urgency of the plea, noting that the film had already been released in theatres and that those interested in watching it had already done so.The petitioner's counsel told the bench that the plea had been registered on November 23 but was yet to be listed for hearing."The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said.The counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film's depiction of the epic. Responding to this, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court."The CJI also remarked, "If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view. Don't waste time of the Court."As the counsel pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayana.Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Its ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.
Article Summary: SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana: Rise of a Legend. Those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective. The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayanas.

Article Title: 'If you offer zero seats, result will be zero': Congress MP Imran Masood's message to SP
Article Text:
Imran takes swipe at Akhilesh's party over seat-sharing

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Friday renewed his criticism of INDIA bloc ally Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh . He questioned the Akhilesh-led party's reluctance to offer the grand old party more seats.Taking a swipe at SP, Saharanpur MP Masood said the Samajwadi Party's tally of 37 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh was made possible in part by Rahul Gandhi's contribution to the INDIA bloc's campaign."It was because of Rahul Gandhi that you (Samajwadi Party)managed to win 37 seats (2024 Lok Sabha Elections). We aren’t saying you didn’t contribute; we are saying that we, too, secured victories. We showed a big heart—but must it always be us who shows a big heart, every single time? Can’t you show a bit more generosity?" he told news agency ANI.The Congress MP also questioned the SP's approach to seat-sharing, saying the party should contest the seats itself if it was unwilling to give them to Congress."If you offer zero seats, the result will naturally be zero. Why don’t you contest these seats yourselves? You go ahead and win them—after all, you claim to have a formula for winnability." he added.Masood's latest remarks came a day after Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge publicly advised him to "talk less and work more", amid concerns that his repeated criticism of the SP could strain ties between the INDIA bloc allies.Addressing party workers at a Constitution Day programme in Lucknow on Thursday, Kharge acknowledged Masood's enthusiasm and his commitment to raising the party's concerns but underlined the importance of collective efforts.“Imran Masood ji bade josh ke saath apni baat rakhte hain. Main roz unhe TV par sunta hoon. Kabhi-kabhi thoda zyada josh mein bhi baat karte hain. Lekin humein baaton se zyada kaam karna hai. Isliye hum jitna milkar kaam karenge, utna hi aage badhenge (Imran Masood ji puts forward his views with great enthusiasm. I hear him regularly on television, where he speaks quite forcefully. But more than statements, we have to work on the ground),” Kharge said.The Congress chief also acknowledged Masood's commitment and his consistent efforts to fight for the party in Parliament.
Article Summary: Congress MP Imran Masood renews his criticism of INDIA bloc ally Samajwadi Party. He questioned the Akhilesh-led party's reluctance to offer the grand old party more seats. Masood's latest remarks came a day after Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge publicly advised him to "talk less and work more"

Article Title: Saurav Das tells Piers Morgan show that he was born in Delhi and is Indian
Article Text:
Das also admitted that he failed his law exam but said he only failed it once, not four times as Ilmi alleged.

TOI Correspondent from London:

Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das told “Piers Morgan Uncensored” on Thursday that he was born in Delhi and he is not Nepalese.He claimed he did not have a birth certificate as a lot of people from his generation didn’t, but said, “I can prove I was born in Delhi.”He said he and his family have spent their whole lives in India. “My mother’s side of the family might have lineage from Nepal, but so do crores of people in India who have come from different nations because in the past we were one,” Das said.BJP national spokesperson Shazia Ilmi alleged on the YouTube show there were three reported discrepancies in Das’s documents — his father’s name, date of birth and place of birth. Later she said: “I am sure he is Indian.”Das denied that his father “had multiple names” and said his date of birth was Jan 15, 1999. He said the show-cause notice issued to him “only mentions place of birth as discrepancy” and he wants to know “where they got the inputs from”. “Is anyone free in India to raise issues against any person on the basis of which passports can be suspended?” he asked.“As far as I am concerned, all my records are the same.”He said he had flown on his current passport twice to Norway last year, and this year to Thailand, and he was facing these “frivolous allegations” now as the government wanted to stop him from spreading the message of the CJP movement outside India.Ilmi said Saurav had a “delusion of grandeur” that he was a great enemy of the Indian government and that “formidable adversaries of the Modi government routinely travel abroad and criticise him”. “Political activism cannot confer immunity from legitimate document verification,” she said.Das also admitted that he failed his law exam but said he only failed it once, not four times as Ilmi alleged.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das told “Piers Morgan Uncensored’ on Thursday that he was born in Delhi and he is not Nepalese. Das also admitted that he failed his law exam but said he only failed it once, not four times as Ilmi alleged.

Article Title: Collegium favouring caste that is 5% of population: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President
Article Text:
The ex-CJI said that in the first four decades of the Supreme Court, that is, till the 1990s, when the SC, through two judgements, took over selection of candidates for appointment as judges to the Supreme Court and high courts, a community (read Brahmins)

Familiarity, networks factors in picking judges, says ex-CJI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ex-CJI B R Gavai on Friday scathingly criticised his successor CJI Surya Kant-led Supreme Court Collegium for ignoring SC, ST, OBC, minority and women candidates and favouring one particular caste -- with just about a 5% population share -- in the appointment of judges to SC & HCs, in complete disregard for the principles of merit and inclusivity, & sought President Droupadi Murmu’s intervention to set things right.Writing an unprecedented three-page letter urging President to hold the Collegium “accountable”, Justice Gavai said that when he headed the collegium, he had ensured that candidates from different sections of society were recommended for appointment as judges.However, in the recent past, disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard for principles of merit and inclusivity. Candidates belonging to one particular section of society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation, to the exclusion of everyone else, including marginalised communities like Scheduled Castes/Tribes, other backward classes, minorities, women and even persons from forward sections of society who are not from a particular community,” former CJI BR Gavai said, adding that the recent use of an unquantifiable metric like demeanour has only aggravated the problem of opacity and favouritism.He did not mention the caste in question, but the ire seemed to be targeted at Brahmins, the caste that CJI Surya Kant belongs to, with Justice Gavai referring to the large share the community has historically enjoyed among members of the higher judiciary.The ex-CJI said that in the first four decades of the Supreme Court, that is, till the 1990s, when the SC, through two judgements, took over selection of candidates for appointment as judges to the Supreme Court and high courts, a community (read Brahmins), then about 1/19th of the population, held over one-third of SC judgeships and lamented that even after 75 years, the pattern persists.The skew in the caste backgrounds of judges has been long debated and has been variously attributed to merit, historical lead of the upper castes, elite affinity and downright casteist bias. Social justice formations have cited this to demand reservation in the judiciary.The Narendra Modi govt also argued for the need to make the judiciary more socially representative while making a push for substituting the Collegium system with the National Judicial Appointments Commission as the recruitment agency for judges. However, it is rare for a former member of the collegium, that too one who served as the CJI, to put the issue so glaringly in the public domain.Lamenting the lack of objectivity and suitability in the process to select judges, the former CJI said it now operates through familiarity, networks and a weird theory of ‘who looks like Supreme Court material’.Ex-CJI Gavai stressed that he was not opposed to meritorious upper-caste candidates getting appointed as judges and only wanted that there must be proportional representation of marginalised communities in Constitutional courts to reflect the country’s social diversity.
Article Summary: Ex-CJI B R Gavai scathingly criticised his successor CJI Surya Kant-led Supreme Court Collegium for ignoring SC, ST, OBC, minority and women candidates. He did not mention the caste in question, but the ire seemed to be targeted at Brahmins, the caste that CJI Kant belongs to.

Article Title: Killing at Rohtak eatery was directed from Georgia: Sleuths
Article Text:
According to sources, gangster Ravi Rathi, a native of Gangnauli village in UP’s Baghpat district and a key associate of jailed gangster Himanshu Bhau, is currently operating from Georgia.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Investigative agencies suspect the brazen quadruple murder at a hotel in Haryana’s Rohtak was orchestrated from Georgia.According to sources, gangster Ravi Rathi, a native of Gangnauli village in UP’s Baghpat district and a key associate of jailed gangster Himanshu Bhau, is currently operating from Georgia.Rathi is reported to have assumed command of the syndicate’s operations following Bhau’s detention in Las Vegas last month. His name also surfaced in an Instagram post by the gang claiming responsibility for the deadly shooting. Agencies are trying to geolocate Rathi and will press for his return to India.Agencies had brought back notorious gangster Venkatesh Garg, a top henchman of UK-based gangster Kapil Sangwan, from Georgia in June this year. Sources said Georgia has been attracting Indian gangsters primarily because it serves as a strategic transit hub with lax entry rules and low enforcement scrutiny.Located at the crossroads of Eastern Europe and Western Asia, it offers easy e-visas or visa-free entry via third-country permits like the UAE or Schengen visas and cheap flights, allowing fugitives to slip in easily and move onward if needed.The shooters were using a less popular, encrypted chat app for communicating with their overseas handlers.The intended target of the attack was rival gangster Sunny Ritoli, who narrowly escaped the ambush.Officers said the assailants had deployed a honeytrap strategy, a known modus operandi of Rathi’s, to lure Ritoli to the spot. A woman, who identified herself as Janhavi, invited Ritoli to the hotel on the pretext of having coffee together.Ritoli was staying at the hotel along with three of the men who were eventually gunned down. Once Ritoli arrived at the venue, the armed assailants struck. While Ritoli managed to flee the scene, his aides died on the spot. The role of the fourth deceased is unconfirmed, with cops suspecting he was ‘collateral damage’.Footage from the hotel shows the assailants arriving at the hotel in a Swift car with a driver. The gunmen were seen entering the eatery brandishing arms, with one of the shooters having concealed his face with a black cloth. With the prime target surviving the latest attempt on his life, agencies remain on high alert for potential retaliatory strikes.
Article Summary: Gangster Ravi Rathi, a native of Gangnauli village in UP’s Baghpat district, is currently operating from Georgia. Rathi is a key associate of jailed gangster Himanshu Bhau. His name also surfaced in an Instagram post by the gang claiming responsibility.

Article Title: CJI had sought probe against Jharkhand high court judge. He is Jharkhand acting chief justice now
Article Text:
Though the CJI’s office routinely receives complaints against sitting judges of various HCs, in Justice Prasad’s case, many complainants provided documentary evidence to back up their charges.

NEW DELHI: In a rare instance, CJI Surya Kant last week asked Jharkhand High Court’s then Chief Justice M S Sonak to probe a spate of complaints questioning the integrity of Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad of the HC.The CJI neither confirmed nor denied receiving a report from Justice Sonak, who is credited with streamlining procedures at the HC after becoming CJ on Jan 9. Justice Sonak retired on Nov 27, and Justice Prasad was appointed acting CJ from Nov 28.Though the CJI’s office routinely receives complaints against sitting judges of various HCs, largely driven by angst of litigants or counsel, in Justice Prasad’s case, many complainants provided documentary evidence to back up their charges.Sources in the Jharkhand government told TOI that complaints against the judge had also reached CM Hemant Soren, who recently requested CJI Kant to look into the concerns.Justice Prasad was appointed to Jharkhand HC on Sept 26, 2014, and transferred six months later to Orissa HC. He was repatriated to Jharkhand HC on Nov 22, 2018. He will retire as an HC judge on June 19, 2029, unless elevated to the SC.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant last week asked Jharkhand High Court’s then Chief Justice M S Sonak to probe a spate of complaints questioning the integrity of Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad of the HC. The CJI neither confirmed nor denied receiving a report from Justice Sonak.

Article Title: 'Modi is not going anywhere': Rajnath hits back at Congress, says only people can remove PM
Article Text:
Singh said PM Modi would continue in office despite oppn's attempts to discredit his leadership.

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday hit back at the Congress , declaring that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was “not going anywhere”, asserting that only the people of India could decide when he should leave office.Addressing a rally after leading the BJP 's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, End Anarchy) foot march, Singh accused the Congress and its allies of attempting to destabilise the country and create an atmosphere of uncertainty in a bid to dislodge Modi from power.Invoking PM Modi's description of himself as a 'faqir', Singh said the prime minister had repeatedly made it clear that he had no personal attachment to power and would leave office whenever the people wanted him to."You must have heard our Prime Minister Modi say on several occasions, 'I am a faqir. When the people say so, I will pick up my bag and leave'," he said.Singh said PM Modi had been entrusted with the responsibility of leading the country by the people and that only they had the authority to take it away."He did not become the Prime Minister because of anyone's inheritance. The people of India gave him this responsibility.And if anyone can take it back, it is only and only the people of India. No one else can do so," he said.Questioning the Congress's attempts to target a prime minister who had secured his position through public support, Singh asked, "Are you trying to remove such a person from power? Are you trying to impose baseless allegations on him?"Issuing a direct challenge to the opposition, Singh said PM Modi would continue in office despite attempts to discredit his leadership."Let the Congress leaders listen carefully. Modi Ji is not going anywhere. I want to convey this message to Congress leaders across the country: Modi Ji is not going anywhere," he said.Taking a further swipe at the Congress, Singh said the party, rather than PM Modi, should prepare to exit the political scene. "The time has come for the Congress to pack up and leave. If anyone has to go, it is the Congress, not Modi," he said, drawing applause from the gathering.The defence minister also contrasted PM Modi's political journey with that of Congress leaders, alleging that political inheritance had shaped the careers of several opposition leaders, while the prime minister had risen through his own journey and public support.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh said PM Modi would continue in office despite attempts to discredit his leadership. Singh accused Congress and its allies of attempting to destabilise the country and create an atmosphere of uncertainty in a bid to dislodge Modi from power.

Article Title: 'Stalin, aka Savarkar 2.0': Vijay's TVK mocks DMK with RSS posts over Centre's delimitation bid
Article Text:
TVK mocks DMK

NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Saturday mocked Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam chief MK Stalin , with a morphed image of him clad in RSS uniform after the party announced its support for Centre's proposed delimitation Bill."Stalin, aka Savarkar 2.0," TVK's IT wing tweeted with the picture.In another animated post, MK Stalin and his son Udhayanidhi Stalin were represented as taking the oath as RRS members."The moment [they] turned completely Sanghi!" it read.The criticism came after DMK decided to support the revised Delimitation Bill in Parliament, with party deputy general secretary and MP A Raja saying the legislation provides for a uniform 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for all states. DMK has 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha.Justifying the party's decision, Stalin described the revised legislation as a major victory for Tamil Nadu 's three-year-long struggle over delimitation. He said the Bill addressed the party's two key demands raised in its 2024 Assembly resolution.The revised proposal does not base delimitation on recent population figures, which the DMK had argued would disproportionately benefit northern states.Instead, it uses the 1971 Census as the basis for determining parliamentary representation.Stalin said the arrangement would allow Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha seats to increase while preserving its existing proportion of representation in Parliament, safeguarding the state's political interests for the next 25 years.The DMK had earlier opposed and defeated a previous version of the Bill, which it had described as hurriedly introduced.
Article Summary: TVK mocked Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam chief MK Stalin with a morphed image of him clad in RSS uniform. The criticism came after DMK decided to support the revised Delimitation Bill in Parliament. DMK has 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha.

Article Title: Election Commission revised SSR timeline for Bengal; clarifies on SIR appeals
Article Text:
This is the second time that the SSR timeline for the state is being extended.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday further revised the schedule for special summary revision (SSR) of the electoral roll in West Bengal, with the draft roll now slated for publication on December 15 and the final roll on February 8, 2027.This is the second time that the SSR timeline for the state is being extended.As per the latest time-table, the polling station rationalisation would be complete by December 3. Claims and objections on the draft roll can be filed between December 15, 2026 and January 14, 2027, followed by their disposal latest by February 1, 2027.In yet another move, EC on Friday wrote to the West Bengal chief electoral officer (CEO), clarifying doubts relating to electors under adjudication by the judicial officers and tribunals appointed to hear appeals against SIR. Breaking up the cases in separate categories, EC clarified that cases of individuals marked 'under adjudication' in draft roll and still showing so as the judicial officers have not given their verdict, shall be referred to the electoral registration officer, who is the statutory authority, for appropriate decision. As for cases marked "under adjudication" that have been decided by the judicial officers but remain pending for e-signature, they may be treated as decided.No action is required regarding individuals who were deleted by judicial officers but have not filed any appeal with the SIR tribunals, said EC. As for individuals who were deleted by the judicial officers and filed appeals with the tribunals that are pending for a decision, these appeals should be prioritised in line with SC directions. EC specifically asked the EROs not to process any Form 6 applications submitted by the individuals until the tribunals give their decision.On what to do with appeals where the tribunal has decided to exclude the appellant from the roll, EC instructed that the said decision must be implemented.The above instructions, EC directed the CEO, may be brought to the notice of all concerned for necessary action and compliance.
Article Summary: The draft roll now slated for publication on December 15 and the final roll on February 8, 2027. This is the second time that the SSR timeline for the state is being extended. As per the latest time-table, the polling station rationalisation would be complete by December 3. Claims and objections on the draft roll can be filed between December 15, 2026 and January 14, 20 27.

Article Title: How obsession with becoming fair is landing many Indians in hospital
Article Text:
Dubious creams that promise quick lightening abound. Many contain mercury at dangerously high levels.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The critical dangers of applying dubious fairness creams came to light last week after a 17-year-old girl from Kerala developed a kidney disorder because of mercury poisoning from one such cream. Nephrologists say it’s not an isolated instance. Unregulated skin-lightening products with unsafe amounts of mercury have been sold and endorsed on social media for a long time, with dark side effects that emerge months later.“Excessive mercury from these creams gets absorbed into the body, leading to membranous nephropathy (MN) in the kidneys. We have seen a few such cases in our OPD,” says AIIMS Delhi nephrologist Dr Sandeep Mahajan.The Kerala girl bought the fairness cream online after seeing how it cleared up her classmates’ skin. “I had severe, painful acne that disappeared after applying the cream. But whenever I stopped using it, the acne returned. So, I continued for almost a year,” she told TOI.Within months, her face became puffy and her feet became swollen, but she kept using the cream till she fell unconscious at home one day. Rushed to hospital, tests revealed MN, in which excessive protein is lost through urine.Doctors suspected the fairness cream she was using, and chemical analysis detected 12,500 parts per million (ppm) of mercury in the product, against a permissible limit of 1 ppm for cosmetics in India, that too, as an unintentional trace component.Mercury is used as an ingredient in fairness creams as it blocks production of the skin-colouring pigment melanin, causing skin tone to lighten. Environmental advocacy firms are pushing for a ban on the sale of such creams.“Unregulated cosmetics aggressively marketed to teens and young adults are a silent public health hazard,” says nephrologist Dr Gouri S of Aster MIMS Mother Hospital, Areekode, who is treating the minor girl. “Consumers must check ingredient lists and certifications before using skincare products and the government must crack down on counterfeit ones.”In 2023, nephrologists at Aster MIMS, Kottakkal, had seen many MN cases, among them a 14-year-old girl whose report showed NELL1 positive, a very rare form of MN. She developed nephrotic syndrome (symptoms caused by damage to the kidneys’ filtering units), perplexing doctors as the only thing she had been doing differently in the past weeks was using a fairness cream. Around the same time, her relative also came to the hospital with foot swelling, a classic nephrotic syndrome symptom. A kidney biopsy showed she too was NELL1 positive. She was also using a fairness cream.“We looked at eight such patients who confirmed using fairness creams,” says Aster MIMS nephrologist Dr Sajeesh Sivadas. Reports showed their mercury and lead levels were over 100 times higher than normal (0.21-1.3 micrograms per litre for mercury and less than 150 for lead). Testing for the NELL-1 antigen in kidney tissue can help doctors rule out heavy metal exposure early on, says Dr Mahajan.Dr Jayant Thomas Mathew, senior consultant nephrologist at Lisie Hospital, Kochi, recalls earlier cases linked to products brought from Dubai, popularly called “Pakistani creams”, where users saw quick skin-lightening results, but some later developed MN with high mercury levels in blood and urine. “Early withdrawal can reverse damage, but delayed treatment may even lead to kidney failure,” he warns.Many cases go unreported as nobody suspects applying a cream can affect internal organs. “Such fairness creams are widely used across age and gender. Once people start using it, they can’t stop due to the rebound pigmentation trap,” says dermatologist Dr Anuradha Kakkanatt Babu.Prolonged use of steroid-based fairness creams can also cause skin thinning, visible blood vessels, redness and sensitivity, adds Dr Kabir Sardana, head of dermatology at RML Hospital, Delhi.“Awareness is key. People need to understand that if there is immediate change in appearance by applying a cream, then something must be wrong,” insists Sujith Kumar, director of Kerala’s drugs control department, which is proposing to make awareness a part of the school curriculum.But it’s easier said than done. “Many people I know are using the cream. Everyone talks about the effects, but no one talks about side effects,” says the 17-year-old girl from Kerala. “I decided to talk about my experience as I don’t want anyone else to suffer my fate.”
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl from Kerala developed a kidney disorder because of mercury poisoning from one such cream. Nephrologists say it’s not an isolated instance. Unregulated skin-lightening products with unsafe amounts of mercury have been sold and endorsed on social media for a long time.

Article Title: 'Both are Congress seats': Imran Masood on SP announcing Saharanpur candidates for UP polls
Article Text:
Imran Masood objects to the SP's candidate announcements for Saharanpur and Behat as seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress continue

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Imran Masood on Saturday objected to the Samajwadi Party announcing candidates for Saharanpur and Behat ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying both seats belong to his party. His remarks came amid ongoing seat-sharing negotiations between the Congress and the Akhilesh Yadav-led party, with uncertainty persisting over the alliance arrangement.“Both those seats belong to the Congress. The Congress won them in 2017. In 2022, the Samajwadi Party won one of them because I had joined the Samajwadi Party. If you look at the electoral equations in those constituencies whenever the Samajwadi Party contested without me, the party had no presence there…Akhilesh ji is a very senior leader. He is a very senior leader and wants to become the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. He will have to show generosity and give us some room,” he said.Congress on Friday said negotiations with the Samajwadi Party were not restricted to the 26 seats initially proposed by the latter. The party said discussions were under way over a list of constituencies it had submitted to the SP earlier this week.The assertion came after a meeting of senior Congress leaders at party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to discuss matters concerning Uttar Pradesh.The Samajwadi Party's decision to announce five candidates while seat-sharing negotiations were underway has added to the uncertainty over the alliance.The SP has played down the announcement, maintaining that it had declared candidates only for seats where its claims were indisputable. The Congress, however, has indicated that such announcements should have been avoided while negotiations were still in progress.During two rounds of discussions with the SP, the Congress had submitted a list of 130 constituencies where it wanted to field candidates.SP president Akhilesh Yadav had said the Congress should focus on winning equations rather than the number of seats, with the objective of ensuring an INDIA bloc victory in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections and paving the way for a change at the Centre in 2029.
Article Summary: Imran Masood objects to the Samajwadi Party announcing candidates for Saharanpur and Behat ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. His remarks came amid ongoing seat-sharing negotiations between the Congress and the Akhilesh Yadav-led party. The Congress has indicated that such announcements should have been avoided while negotiations were still in progress.

Article Title: From a knowledge giver to a seeker
Article Text: There are innings that rewrite history. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ’s 204 off just 53 balls recently belongs among them. At 15, he has achieved what seasoned cricketers dream of; an astonishing exhibition of timing and talent.What makes it more fascinating is what preceded it. Vaibhav had not been at his best against New Zealand. What brought about the change? A 30-minute conversation with Yuvraj Singh before the match where the senior offered technical pointers and urged him to spend time at the crease. The youngster listened, watched videos of his earlier batting and returned with a renewed perspective. Perhaps the magic lay less in what was said than in what was received. The chemistry between an exceptional teacher and a receptive student is an alchemy known only to the two. Sometimes, great lessons need few words. Guru Dakshinamurthy’s lesson to the four sages, after all, was imparted through silence.In our tradition, the teacher-student relationship is sacred. A worthy student searches for a great teacher; a great teacher, too, yearns for the right disciple. A rain cloud seeks parched earth to nourish. So does a realised master seek a receptive mind in which wisdom can take root and its lineage continue.A true seeker approaches with an empty cup, free of ego and preconceptions. In a Zen story, a king seeks knowledge from a master who pours tea into his cup even after it overflows. The king protests. The master says, “You are filled with your own convictions. As no more tea can enter this cup, no teaching can enter a mind filled with its own ideas. Empty the cup and come.”I am reminded of MogaMul, a Tamil novel by Thi Janakiraman. Babu, a college student gifted in music, is taken to Ranganna, a distinguished musician. Reluctant to accept students, Ranganna believes it is difficult to make them unlearn what they have learnt elsewhere. Yet he accepts Babu.Soon, Ranganna awaits his pupil each morning. When Babu misses a class, he tells him, “I have been waiting like an old bird. If you are not coming, can’t you send word?” Babu thinks his master is displeased with his indiscipline. Later, he understands that Ranganna genuinely misses him. That affection transforms him. Music is no longer preparation for concerts; it becomes his destination. He is no longer merely learning. He is seeking.Valluvar captures the soul-stirring experience in Kural 718:“Unarvadhu Udayaarmun Sollal ValarvadhanPaaththiyul Neer Sorindhatru.”“To part knowledge before one who absorbs isLike irrigating in a fertile soil”In the Mahabharata, there is an instance where a gust extinguishes the lamp as the disciples eat. Arjuna continues eating in the dark. Drona points out how the hand instinctively finds the mouth even without light. That observation triggers Arjuna: if the hand finds its destination in darkness, why cannot an arrow find its mark? He begins practising archery at night. The seed is planted by the guru; the discipline belongs to the student. No word of Drona’s wisdom is lost on Arjuna.Perhaps this is the secret of every great teacher-student relationship. When they meet, learning transcends instruction. It becomes a shared journey of embellishing knowledge and growth, where both lives are shimmering. Sometimes, 30 minutes with the right guru can change a lifetime. Sometimes, silence is enough.
Article Summary: The chemistry between an exceptional teacher and a receptive student is an alchemy known only to the two. Sometimes, great lessons need few words. When they meet, learning transcends instruction. It becomes a shared journey of embellishing knowledge and growth.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

The Buffalo Bills had plenty to celebrate after edging out Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving. But away from the result, their new $2.1 billion home became the centre of an unexpected controversy. Videos shared online appeared to show water collecting inside parts of Highmark Stadium, with some footage raising questions about possible leaks and drainage. For a venue built to deliver a modern NFL experience, the scenes were difficult to ignore. Fans quickly turned their attention from the game to the stadium itself.The Thanksgiving matchup brought challenging weather to Buffalo, with heavy rain and strong winds affecting conditions throughout the evening. While the players battled on the field, footage from inside the stadium began circulating on social media. Some clips appeared to show water gathering in public areas, while others prompted concerns about dripping water and how well the venue handled the downpour.The timing made the criticism even sharper. The new Highmark Stadium opened in August 2026 after a reported investment of around $2.1 billion. Expectations were naturally high for a project of that scale.Fans expect more than impressive architecture from a new NFL venue. They also want a comfortable and reliable place to watch games, particularly when the weather turns unpleasant.The stadium features a partial canopy, but its open-air design leaves the playing field exposed. That decision has now returned to the spotlight, with supporters questioning whether the venue should have included a retractable roof.The debate is not limited to the videos showing apparent water problems. The stadium's ability to handle severe weather has also become a talking point. Local weather coverage described persistent rain and strong winds around the venue, creating difficult conditions for spectators and players.There is also a wider question about the money involved. A retractable roof would have added to the construction cost, but the current situation has led some fans to revisit whether that investment would have been worthwhile.On the field, Buffalo managed to overcome the conditions and secure a 13-10 victory over Kansas City. The result gave Bills supporters a Thanksgiving win, but the stadium controversy quickly became another talking point.For a venue that represents such a major investment, the viral footage has created an uncomfortable first impression during a high-profile weather test. However, the clips alone do not establish a structural defect, and the reported leaks still need proper verification. The Bills and stadium authorities may now face growing pressure to explain what happened and whether any improvements are needed.
Article Summary: Highmark Stadium's open-air design sparks criticism during Chiefs game. Videos shared online appear to show water collecting inside parts of venue. Bills beat Kansas City 13-10 on Thanksgiving, but controversy reigns. Fans question whether the venue should have included a retractable roof.

Article Title: What is Marc Marquez's net worth after eight MotoGP titles? Inside his career earnings, luxury home and sponsorship empire
Article Text:
​What Is Marc Marquez's Net Worth in 2026? (Getty Images)​

Marc Marquez net worth and career earnings

Sponsors, property and how Marquez handles money

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Marc Marquez retires with an estimated net worth of $75 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. The 33-year-old announced the decision on Friday, five days after clinching a record-equaling eighth MotoGP title in Portugal. It also ties him with Giacomo Agostini for the most premier-class crowns. Sunday's Valencia Grand Prix will be his last race. He is leaving a Ducati contract that ran through 2028, extended only in June. Over his career he earned an estimated $125 million to $175 million before taxes and expenses, though none of these figures are official.The $75 million figure is an estimate, and the career earnings range is wide for a reason. MotoGP contracts are private. Teams rarely publish numbers, so outlets lean on paddock talk and Spanish media reports. What is clear is that Honda paid the most. In February 2020, Marquez signed a four-year extension covering 2021 to 2024. Ducati sporting director Paolo Ciabatti said at the time it was worth between €15 million and €20 million a year, which puts the whole deal at €60 million to €80 million.Marquez never collected all of it. After 11 seasons he left Honda a year early, giving up the final year of that deal.At Gresini in 2024, he has said, he took no team salary at all. He wanted to win again, and money was not the reason.The pay returned with Ducati's factory team in 2025. Autosport put his base salary at roughly €3 million, far below his Honda money. His 11 Grand Prix wins that year brought in more than €2 million in incentives alone, according to the same report. The contract terms were never made public.Away from the track, Marquez has long-running personal deals with Red Bull, Estrella Galicia, Shoei and Alpinestars. His number 93, taken from his birth year, sits on clothing and merchandise. He also has stakes in real estate, audiovisual production, hospitality and talent management, including Vertical Management, which he shares with his brother Álex.He has been unusually open about his finances. On a Spanish podcast he said his bonus for the 2013 title topped €1 million. More than half went to taxes and 10% to his manager. He added that he has always paid taxes in Spain, even while owning a second home in Andorra.His main home is a mansion in Pozuelo de Alarcón, near Madrid. He values it at about €10 million and says it is fully paid off. The one flashy purchase, a Porsche 911 Turbo S, was sold after roughly 4,000 kilometers because the look of it made him uncomfortable.None of that explains the exit, and Marquez did not try to. "The reason for my retirement? I think we don't need any reasons sometimes," he said in Valencia. Walking away also meant leaving two more Ducati seasons on the table. He chose to stop.
Article Summary: Marc Marquez retires with an estimated net worth of $75 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. The 33-year-old announced the decision on Friday, five days after clinching a record-equaling eighth MotoGP title. Sunday's Valencia Grand Prix will be his last race.

Article Title: ‘If you people are not afraid, can I afford to be afraid?’: Diljit Dosanjh thanks fans for showing up at Mumbai concert despite threat
Article Text:
Dosanjh is next scheduled to perform in Bengaluru on Sunday as part of his AURA India Tour 2026. (Photo credit: Instagram)

Over 500 cops deployed after threat email

From 'Clash' to 'Main Hoon Punjab', fans sing along

(With agency inputs)





MUMBAI: “If you people are not afraid, can I afford to be afraid?” Actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh asked fans at his Mumbai concert on Friday, thanking them for turning up despite bomb threats and praising the police for the security arrangements at Mahalaxmi Racecourse.Addressing the crowd midway through the show, Dosanjh said the threats appeared aimed at frightening people and keeping them away from his concerts. He said their willingness to attend despite the threats gave him the courage to perform.“Their only objective is to ensure that people do not attend Diljit's show, to frighten them, threaten them and stop them by any means possible. I don't know why this is happening to me, day after day. From my side, there is only love for you, even if you throw bombs,” he said.In a video shared on Instagram, the singer also thanked the Mumbai Police , acknowledging that security checks were causing delays for concertgoers outside the venue.“I know that as many people are here inside, there are that many people stranded outside. The police personnel are helpless too; they are checking everyone before allowing them in. My heartfelt thanks to the Mumbai Police,” he said.Dosanjh also recalled the difficulties he faced during his 2024 performances, saying that being able to hold a concert itself had become stressful in 2026.“When I performed in 2024, I felt I was being troubled quite a bit. I was asked not to sing this song or that song, and so on. But those were only small things. At this point in 2026, simply managing to hold my show is a cause for stress in itself,” he said.More than 500 Mumbai Police personnel were deployed at Mahalaxmi Racecourse for the concert after an email received on Thursday threatened blasts, grenade attacks and the planting of improvised explosive devices at the mayor's office, Metro stations and Dosanjh's show.The email, received on the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 terror attacks, also referred to Khalistan and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. It threatened violence linked to a programme involving Dosanjh and people associated with the event.Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad teams swept the venue, while entry checks were conducted at all five gates instead of the earlier three. Private security personnel, dog squads and an Anti-Narcotics Cell team were also deployed.A no-car zone extending 500 to 700 metres around the racecourse was enforced, with no parking allowed at the venue. Organisers had also been instructed not to disclose details of the singer's hotel or arrival time.The concert began around 8pm and continued for nearly two hours, with Dosanjh performing songs including 'Clash', 'Hass Hass', 'Vibe', 'Pokito' and 'Kinni Kinni', along with fan favourites such as 'Saanson Ki Maala', 'Ikk Kudi' and 'Bhool Bhulaiyya'.The singer also spoke about the influence of his village roots on his music. “The songs I sing are about villages, and I come from a village myself. Even if you do not understand my songs, you will surely sense the fragrance of the soil,” he said.He closed the show with 'Main Hoon Punjab', as thousands of fans sang along.Dosanjh is next scheduled to perform in Bengaluru on Sunday as part of his AURA India Tour 2026. A bomb threat has also been reported ahead of that concert, with police registering a case after an email warned of a possible explosion at the venue and a nearby Metro station.His India tour has faced similar threats before, including ahead of his November 15 Indore concert, when emails were sent to the mayor's office, private schools and the Gwalior bench of the Madhya Pradesh high court.
Article Summary: Dosanjh thanks fans for turning up despite bomb threats at his Mumbai concert. More than 500 Mumbai Police personnel deployed at Mahalaxmi Racecourse. Email received on Thursday threatened blasts, grenade attacks and the planting of improvised explosive devices at the mayor's office and Metro stations.

Article Title: Sambhal woman quoted Rs 2 lakh for IVF at Moradabad nursing home alleges negligence, UP consumer commission orders two doctors and Shubham Nursing Home to pay Rs 10 lakh with 9% interest
Article Text:
Woman claimed medical negligence during her test tube procedure (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)





LUCKNOW: Moradabad district consumer disputes redressal commission (I) has imposed a fine on two doctors and a nursing home for medical negligence. The court ordered the defendants to pay Rs 10 lakh plus nine percent annual interest.The commission also ordered Rs 15,000 for mental, physical, and financial damages, and an additional Rs 10,000 as litigation expenses. Bashra, a resident of Sarai Tareen in Sambhal district, filed a petition with the district consumer disputes redressal commission (I) through her lawyer.She stated that due to her infertility, she had contacted the doctors at Shubham Nursing Home, located at Pilikothi Square in Civil Lines, to conceive a child through test tube technology.The doctors admitted her to the hospital, quoting a cost of Rs two lakh. The woman has alleged negligence during her treatment.After hearing the case, commission chairman Rama Shankar Singh and member Ruchika Saraswat found Shubham Nursing Home and two doctors guilty and imposed fines.The commission ordered the opposing team to pay 9% interest on Rs 10 lakh within one month from the date of filing the complaint, September 30, 2022, until the payment.
Article Summary: Moradabad district consumer disputes redressal commission (I) has imposed a fine on two doctors and a nursing home for medical negligence. The court ordered the defendants to pay Rs 10 lakh plus nine percent annual interest. The commission also ordered Rs 15,000 for mental, physical, and financial damages.

Article Title: A Chandigarh woman on her way to receive 'Best Advocate Award' was left waiting for nearly two hours after her booked cab failed to arrive; consumer commission orders travel agency to pay Rs 10,000
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

5 key highlights





CHANDIGARH: A cab that never arrived cost a Chandigarh woman nearly two hours on the morning she was supposed to travel to Ludhiana for an award ceremony. With no response from the travel agency, she had to find another vehicle to make the journey. The incident dates back to August 28, 2022. Nearly four years later, a Punjab consumer commission has held the travel agency responsible for failing to provide the promised service and ordered it to pay Rs 10,000 in compensation and litigation expenses.The dispute centred on a booking made three days before the scheduled journey. The woman had contacted the agency on August 25 to arrange a Chandigarh-Ludhiana round trip. She was due to attend a function in Ludhiana, where she was reportedly set to receive the Best Advocate Award. The fare became part of the dispute. While the agency initially quoted Rs 2,200, the woman negotiated it down to Rs 2,000, an arrangement reflected in their WhatsApp conversation. She claimed that she had also paid Rs 1,000 in advance and was assured that the cab would pick her up from her residence at 6.30 am.That assurance was not honoured. When the vehicle failed to arrive, the woman tried reaching the agency but allegedly received no information about the delay.After waiting for around two hours, she made alternative transport arrangements and continued to Ludhiana. She subsequently approached the consumer commission, alleging harassment and embarrassment caused by the agency's failure. The agency disputed her version, arguing that the booking was never confirmed because she had not deposited 50% of the agreed fare as advance. It maintained that its representative had shared the number of an independent cab driver on August 27 and instructed her to contact him directly. It also denied receiving the Rs 1,000 payment or assuring her of a confirmed pickup.The commission's examination of the WhatsApp messages established that the two parties had discussed and agreed on the booking and fare. While the woman could not produce evidence of the alleged advance payment, the commission found that the agency could not deny that a cab had been booked but was not provided on time. The woman had also sought relief on the ground that she missed an important award ceremony. However, the commission noted that she had submitted no documentary evidence to establish that she was actually scheduled to receive the award or had missed the function.It nevertheless held that the absence of proof regarding the award did not excuse the agency's failure to provide the vehicle at the promised time. The commission partly allowed her complaint and directed the travel agency to pay Rs 10,000 towards deficiency in service, mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses within 30 days.1. A Chandigarh woman booked a cab for a Chandigarh-Ludhiana round trip on August 28, 2022, to attend an award ceremony, where she was reportedly scheduled to receive the Best Advocate Award.2. The travel agency initially quoted Rs 2,200 but agreed to Rs 2,000 after negotiations on WhatsApp. The woman claimed she also paid Rs 1,000 in advance and was assured of a 6.30 am pickup.3. When the cab failed to arrive and the agency allegedly did not respond, the woman waited for nearly two hours before arranging alternative transport to reach Ludhiana.4. The agency denied confirming the booking, claiming she had not paid the required 50% advance. The consumer commission, however, found that WhatsApp messages established that the booking and fare had been discussed and agreed upon.5. The Punjab consumer commission held the agency guilty of deficiency in service and ordered it to pay Rs 10,000 towards compensation, mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses within 30 days. It noted that the woman had not provided documentary proof that she was due to receive the award or had missed the ceremony.
Article Summary: A cab that never arrived cost a Chandigarh woman nearly two hours on the morning she was supposed to travel to Ludhiana for an award ceremony. Article Title: 'I love someone else': Day before engagement, father kills daughter who rejected groom chosen by family; hangs body to fake suicide
Article Text:
A woman named A Kalyani was reportedly killed by her father in Adilabad for refusing an arranged marriage





HYDERABAD: A day before her betrothal, an 18-year-old woman in Adilabad allegedly told her family that she did not want marry the man they had chosen for her as she was in love with another man.Hours later, her father allegedly smothered her to death while she slept, hanged her body from a roof beam to pass it off as suicide and hurriedly cremated the body before relatives could arrive, police said.Police arrested accused Kailash on Thursday after questioning. The woman, A Kalyani, was killed at the family’s home in Umri village in Adilabad in the early hours of Nov 24, police said.Cops first became suspicious over the haste with which the family conducted the last rites. Narnoor police had received an alert from Umri residents around 8.30 am on Nov 24 about Kalyani’s suspicious death.“By the time our team reached the village, the cremation was almost completed. The woman’s father claimed that she hanged herself at home and they noticed the body at 5.30 am. We became suspicious since the family tried to finish the final rites without waiting for relatives within three hours after her death.Also, in their community, unmarried deceased are buried and not cremated as per custom,” Adilabad district SP Akhil Mahajan said.Umri panchayat secretary B Rajanna had lodged a complaint with Narnoor police a day after her death, stating that Kalyani’s marriage had been fixed and her engagement was scheduled for Nov 25. He alleged that she was in love with another man and Kailash killed her fearing the affair would bring disgrace to his family.Police registered a murder case under Section 103(1) of the BNS.Utnoor additional SP Ruthwik Sai Kotte said Kalyani had told her family on the night of Nov 23 that she was not interested in the proposed marriage because she was in love with another man.“Kailash felt that his daughter’s decision might bring disrepute to the family and smothered her to death during the early hours of Nov 24 when she was asleep,” the ASP said.Police said Kailash then tied a stole around his daughter’s neck and hanged her body from a roof beam inside the house in an attempt to make the death appear to be suicide.“During interrogation, Kailash confessed to killing his daughter. We arrested and remanded him on Thursday,” the SP said.
Article Summary: 18-year-old A Kalyani was reportedly killed by her father in Adilabad for refusing an arranged marriage. Her father allegedly smothered her to death while she slept, hanged her body from a roof beam to pass it off as suicide.

Article Title: Coffee machine explodes ahead of AAP rally in Punjab's Moga; 1 critical
Article Text:
A man reportedly sustained fatal injuries after a coffee machine exploded at the venue.





CHANDIGARH: A hospitality worker was critically injured after the compressor of a coffee-making machine exploded at a food stall set up for media personnel ahead of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) rally in Moga, Punjab , on Thursday.The worker, whose identity was not immediately known, had been hired by the contractor to serve refreshments to media personnel at the stall.The incident took place around 10.30am, when relatively few people were present inside the food stall. According to eyewitnesses, a thick cloud of smoke billowed from the machine following the explosion, reducing visibility inside the tent for a few moments. The blast also ripped apart a portion of the tent.The worker was pulled out and rushed for medical attention. He was reported to be in critical condition.A medical team and forensic personnel also reached the spot following the explosion.

Ireland are set to make history in January 2027 when their men's side tours Pakistan for the first time, with a six-match 50-over series scheduled in Lahore as part of their preparations for the ICC World Cup Qualifier.Cricket Ireland on Thursday confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9 for a series running from January 13 to 24, with all six matches to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore.The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The matches will be played on January 13, 15 and 17 against the Shaheens, before the two teams meet in the ODIs on January 20, 22 and 24. Match timings are yet to be confirmed.While this will be the first visit to Pakistan by the Ireland men's side, it will not be the first tour by an Irish cricket team. The Ireland women's side visited the country in 2022 and famously won the T20I series.The six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February 2027, which will be held in South Africa and Namibia.Graeme West, Cricket Ireland's Director of High Performance, underlined the importance of the tour in providing the one-day squad with valuable match practice ahead of the qualification campaign.“This is an extremely important tour for our One-Day squad as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifiers in February. Following the nine games played in the second half of 2026, a further six 50-over matches against quality opponents will support the players readiness for the qualifier taking place in South Africa and Namibia.“While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027.“Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope.”The Pakistan Cricket Board had initially planned a triangular series involving Ireland, Pakistan and Zimbabwe. However, Zimbabwe subsequently withdrew, citing its inability to travel to Pakistan. The revised arrangement will see Ireland play two separate three-match assignments instead.Ireland and Pakistan have faced each other seven times in men's ODIs, with Pakistan winning five matches, Ireland claiming one victory and one encounter ending in a tie.Ireland's only win remains one of the most memorable results in its cricketing history. It came during the 2007 World Cup in the Caribbean, when Ireland stunned Pakistan to knock the former champions out of the tournament.Pakistan, meanwhile, will enter the series after winning the ODI tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi and Lahore last month, under the captaincy of Shaheen Shah Afridi The six-match series will also offer Pakistan valuable preparation ahead of its international assignments in 2027, including the ODI World Cup later in the year.
Article Summary: Cricket Ireland confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9. The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February.

Article Title: 'We've got ourselves into a hole': Dinesh Karthik slams India's catching as batting collapse puts follow-on in sight
Article Text:
Glimpses of India's dropped catches in the Christchurch Test. (Video grabs)

Dropped catches come back to haunt India

'India need to bat out that first session'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's troubles in the Christchurch Test against New Zealand have gone beyond their batting woes, with former India wicketkeeper-batter Dinesh Karthik pointing to the team's shoddy catching as a major reason behind their precarious position. Karthik believes India's fielding lapses allowed New Zealand to post a competitive first-innings total before another batting collapse left the visitors staring at the possibility of a follow-on.India ended the second day's play at 116/6 in reply to New Zealand's 356 at Hagley Oval, still trailing by 240 runs with only four wickets remaining. Dhruv Jurel was unbeaten on seven, with Akash Deep yet to join him at the crease.With India struggling to stay in the contest, Karthik questioned the team's catching standards and warned that their hopes of reaching the World Test Championship (WTC) final were also taking a hit."What is happening with India's catching? Out of the 12 Test playing nations, India is 8th right now. We are harbouring ambitions to go to the World Test Championship final. But if you're 8th, then you've dropped a lot of catches, you've let go of a lot of crucial moments and that basically means your chances of getting to that final is going to be next to impossible," Karthik said in a video on his Instagram account on Saturday.India paid a heavy price for their fielding lapses, particularly against New Zealand's middle order. Captain Tom Latham was dropped on 29 on the opening day before going on to score 59, while wicketkeeper-batter Tom Blundell survived a chance on 49 in the gully.Blundell made the most of the reprieve, top-scoring for New Zealand with 89. Akash Deep was particularly unlucky, with three catches going down off his bowling before he eventually completed his five-wicket haul by dismissing Matt Henry.Karthik felt India's inability to convert even straightforward chances had undermined their bowling effort."In general, one of the reasons why most test teams do well is because their close-in catchers are solid. They convert half chances and create more opportunities than what is available. Now India have gone the other way round. They're dropping sitters and that's come back to bite them," he added.The fielding mistakes were followed by another batting collapse as New Zealand's seamers exploited the movement and extra bounce on offer. While Rishabh Pant fell attempting an ambitious shot against Jacob Duffy, KL Rahul was caught at point after going for an uncharacteristic drive.With India losing six wickets and still trailing by 240 runs, Karthik warned that the follow-on was a very real possibility."Eventually, India is so far behind in this test match, 240 runs to go, just four wickets in hand in the first innings. We're looking at basically New Zealand putting us in and taking a follow on."We've got ourselves into a hole. India need to bat out that first session, try and reduce the deficit to 150. If that doesn't happen, India are going to find it really hard to come back in this Test match," said Karthik.The former India batter acknowledged that some of the dismissals were questionable but defended Pant's attacking instincts, pointing to his record in Test cricket."A lot of shots are questionable. I mean, we can say that they play good shots but today, most of the shots backfired and they look back at those replays and be like, was that shot the right one?"But when it comes to Rishabh Pant, I think he averages mid-40s and somewhere on this pitch, we need to give him the relevance to go after those big shots. I know a lot of you are going to come back and say the situation and everything."But every time he plays these shots, he's been successful in Test cricket because he has the courage to do it and the conviction and the consistency to a large part. It's always debatable but for me, the bigger picture is catches and we did drop too many," he concluded.
Article Summary: Dinesh Karthik says India's fielding lapses have cost them in Christchurch Test. Former India wicketkeeper-batter points to team's shoddy catching as a major reason behind their precarious position. India ended the second day's play at 116/6 in reply to New Zealand's 356 at Hagley Oval, still trailing by 240 runs with only four wickets remaining.

Article Title: A Georgia teenager began cooking for his family after his mother died; his home-cooking videos have now attracted more than two million social media followers
Article Text:
Image via Chefjoeycharney/ Instagram

A chicken soup recipe that tastes extra special because it is your grandma’s recipe or a cookie recipe that only your dad knows. Everyone has different ways of expressing love, and some just make delicious food instead of saying it aloud. Sometimes, a cooking lesson by your mom can make for the most special memories and sharing a meal with family can feel more fulfilling than a vacation. This idea was the reason for the sudden popularity of a teenage boy from Georgia who started cooking after his mother got sick.Joey Charney (@chefjoeycharney) became internet famous with more than a million followers. The 18-year-old boy has never had formal culinary training nor has he worked in a restaurant ever, yet he is making meals for his family in his home kitchen. He attracted millions of followers when he shared the story of how he started cooking for his large family when his mom, Jennifer, became ill with breast cancer.Joey's mother, Jennifer, was a stay-at-home mom of eight. She fought breast cancer for ten years, and as her illness progressed the kids took over more and more of what she used to do. Joey, the youngest son, volunteered to cook, though he knew very little about it.However, he had the support of his mother who used to guide him from the other room.Joey could ask his mom questions, and from her bed she'd sniff out trouble and call out that something was burning. His answer, he recalled to Newsweek, was a cheerful shout back: "I got it! I got it!"Along the way, Joey documented his cooking journey online, openly sharing the ups and downs of feeding his family. His videos were not glossy, high-resolution productions, but rather a day-to-day documentation of his journey with his mom. The videos displayed pure human emotions of grief, happiness and the ups & downs of life. This is what appealed to the people on the internet.Jennifer lived long enough to see him pass 100,000 TikTok followers, a milestone that left her astonished and proud. Newsweek reports he now has roughly 1.5 million followers on TikTok and more than a million on Instagram.After Jennifer's death on August 7, 2026, at the age of 53, a post from Joey drew heartfelt replies. Many celebrity chefs reached out to help, brands offered to send products to help the family through the process and ordinary people sent heartfelt messages for Joey and his family during such a difficult time. Celebrity model Bella Hadid commented “We love you, Joey” on the post where he announced his mom’s death.Joey told CBS News he's happy with where he is but not with the reason he got there. That sentence may be the most grown-up thing in the whole story. He doesn't pretend the loss was secretly a gift, nor does he turn down the good that came from it.Anyone who has tried to recreate a parent's signature dish will understand this. When CBS News asked what he misses most, Joey said he misses everything about his mom, her cooking especially. One dish that he mentioned specifically was her Parmesan chicken which he says he can’t get the “same way.”But his biggest test came with the big Thanksgiving meal. As reported by CBS News, this was the family’s first Thanksgiving without Jennifer and was a big change for the family. However, Joey was already preparing. He roasted a couple of whole chickens that week as practice.One of Jennifer’s recipes has stayed with Joey which he tells Newsweek “will hold a permanent spot on Thanksgiving and Christmas,” but especially in his heart are the Hello Dolly bars. His mom discovered the recipe in a magazine long ago. Soon, the cookie bars involving coconut, chocolate and pecan nuts became a family favourite according to Joey.He knows how exhausting the job is. Newsweek reports that last year he cooked all day for the family but was too tired to eat. This year the guest list includes his dad, seven siblings, a sister-in-law, grandparents, an uncle and cousins.
Article Summary: Joey Charney, 18, became internet famous with more than a million followers. He started cooking for his large family when his mom, Jennifer, became ill with breast cancer. He has never had formal culinary training nor has he worked in a restaurant ever, yet he is making meals for his family.

Article Title: Trapped in fishing nets off Vadhvan coast, 2 dolphins rescued & released into sea
Article Text:
Trapped in fishing nets off Vadhvan coast, 2 dolphins rescued & released into sea

Palghar

:





Two dolphins trapped in fishing nets off the Vadhvan coast in Dahanu were rescued and safely released into the sea on Friday morning. The dolphins were likely carried close to the shore by incoming tidal waters and then got entangled in nets laid by fishermen. Local fishermen, who had ventured into the sea for their routine fishing activity, noticed two dolphins struggling in their nets. Realising the urgency, they alerted the authorities. The forest department and a wildlife rescue team rushed to the spot and launched a rescue operation with the help of locals. The nets were carefully removed without causing any injury to the dolphins. Both were subsequently released into deeper waters and they returned to their natural habitat. The prompt response by the fishermen, forest officials and rescue team has drawn appreciation from locals and environmental enthusiasts. The fishermen’s willingness to prioritise the safety of marine life despite the possible damage to their nets has also been widely appreciated.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai gang poses as FDA officers, threatens paan shop owner with gutkha case to extort Rs 2.66 lakh
Article Text:
Five men posing as FDA officers extorted Rs 2.66 lakh from a paan shop owner in Navi Mumbai (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)

NAVI MUMBAI: The APMC police have arrested five members of a gang of fraudsters who had posed as FDA officers and extorted Rs 2.66 lakh from a paan shop owner residing in Kopri village Vashi node after threatening legal action by claiming that he was selling banned gutkha and violating FDA norms.The arrested accused have been identified as Prashant Shinde, Satyendra Rastogi, Atharva Bhosale, Prathamesh Gaikwad and Ankush Pawar.While, their aide Umesh Kodag is being searched informed Abasaheb Patil, senior inspector of APMC police station.SPI Patil informed that on November 4 around 6pm, four members of the gang posing as FDA officers had gone to the residence of the Paan shop owner identified as Abhilash Pandey, 35, residing in Datta Krupa society, Kopri village.Reportedly, they showed fake ID card of an organization namely 'Food and Drug Consumer Welfare Committee' and conducted his house search. As they could not find any gutkha products, they took him in their SUV under pretext of an inquiry."Inside the SUV, they assaulted him and forced him to make online payment of Rs 1.86 lakh. Thereafter, they made him to call his wife and arrange Rs 80,000 as random for releasing him. One accused went to Pandey's residence and collected the ransom amount.However, Pandey lodged a police complaint after nine days on November 13 and an FIR was registered under BNS sections for kidnapping, robbery, criminal intimidation, impersonating public servant and house trespass among other criminal offences," Patil said.He informed that initially, the four accused who had executed the crime were arrested gradually from different areas in Koparkhairane and Ghansoli on November 14 and 15. They led to one more accused who was arrested on November 15.So far five accused have been arrested and one identified accused Umesh Kodag is being traced. All arrested acused have been remanded to magistrate custody.SPI Patil said, "The SUV used in the crime has been seized and it is registered in the name of the wife of the arrested accused Prashant Shinde. The SUV was adorned with a MNS party flag, to intimidate victims, Shinde was previously a MNS party office bearer."
Article Summary: Five men posing as FDA officers extorted Rs 2.66 lakh from a paan shop owner in Navi Mumbai. They threatened legal action by claiming that he was selling banned gutkha and violating FDA norms. The arrested accused have been identified as Prashant Shinde, Satyendra Rastogi, Atharva Bhosale, Prathamesh Gaikwad and Ankush Pawar.

Article Title: Panvel police trace auto driver through CCTV, recover woman's bag with gold and Rs 1.18 lakh cash

NAVI MUMBAI: A 62-year-old woman from Pen in Raigad district got back her handbag containing 75 grams of gold ornaments, Rs 1.18 lakh in cash and a mobile phone, collectively worth Rs 11.50 lakh, within 10 hours of reporting its loss to Panvel City police on November 13.Archana Arun Jadhav had lost the bag while travelling in an autorickshaw from Panvel railway station to the bus depot to visit her brother for Bhau Beej. The bag had apparently fallen on the road.Senior inspector Bala Kumbhar said API Sachin Powar and his team scanned CCTV footage along the route and spotted an autorickshaw driver picking up the bag. By tracking the vehicle through multiple cameras, the police traced its driver, Raju Ganpat Sawant (63), to his residence and recovered the valuables.Sawant told police that he had picked up the bag after seeing it fall from an autorickshaw around 1 pm near Panvel railway station. He claimed he intended to hand it over to the police but was delayed by personal commitments. He said he had kept the valuables safely, hoping their owner would trace him.The police returned the belongings to Jadhav, who praised them for their prompt action.
